tagline: Watch security work, step by step.

home.lead: Every topic is a timeline you can play, pause, scrub and inspect. Attacker action on one side, the wire in the middle, the logs a SOC would see on the other.
home.actorBody: What the attacker or the user does, step by step, with the reason for each move.
home.wireBody: What crosses the network, decoded field by field and byte by byte, with a plain-language note on every field.
home.defenderBody: The logs, alerts and telemetry the same step produces, from the sources a SOC actually reads.
home.domainsLead: A canonical topic lives once and is referenced wherever it is needed. Each domain opens as a map, so you see a path rather than a list.
home.safetyBody: Every scenario uses synthetic data. No lesson carries working exploit code or operational attack instructions, and every attack lesson ends in its detection counterpart.

about.title: About SecViz
about.intentBody: SecViz teaches security by animating how it happens. Rather than describing a handshake or an attack path, it plays one: you pause at any moment and take the artifact apart field by field, then look at the same moment from the defender's side.
about.safetyBody: All scenarios use synthetic data. There are no live targets, no real credentials and no working exploit payloads anywhere in this platform. Attack lessons exist to build detection and defence understanding: each one names the detection lesson that answers it, and the attack is shown at the level of what it looks like on the wire and in the logs, not as a procedure to follow.
about.howBody: One component, the Scenario Player, drives every lesson. A lesson is data validated against a schema, so a contributor adds one without touching engine code. Panels stay synchronised to a single timeline: the stage animates the current step, the decode panel takes apart that step's artifact, and the telemetry panel shows what it produced.
about.accessBody: The player is fully keyboard-driven: space plays and pauses, the arrow keys step. Colour is never the only signal, every meaning carries a marker or a label as well, and both themes meet WCAG AA contrast. Where the system asks for reduced motion the player switches to step-through mode with no continuous animation.
about.creditBody: The interaction model here is modelled on Protocol Explorer by Dilum Sanjaya, which teaches networking by animating packets and decoding every one byte by byte. SecViz applies that pedagogy across security and adds the defender view.

footer.simulated: All data on this platform is simulated.
